```{r setup-mascot_example, include = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
studio_character <- if (exists("studio_character")) studio_character else formals(mascot::mascot)$character
```

```{r mascot_example-try-live, echo = FALSE}
if (!in_studio()) guide_try_live("mascot_example")
```

### Copy an example into your project

Find the names with `r guide_fn_link("mascot_examples")`, then locate an app
without starting a server:

```r
basename(mascot::mascot_example("form-check", run = FALSE))
```

The call returns `app.R`. To adapt this single-file example, copy that file into
your project:

```r
path <- mascot::mascot_example("form-check", run = FALSE)
file.copy(path, "app.R", overwrite = FALSE)
```

Choose a destination without an existing `app.R`. For the multi-file examples
(`"studio"`, `golem` and the rhino-shaped one), copy the whole containing folder instead so
that their supporting files stay together. The `golem` example needs golem;
the single-file scenarios need Shiny, bslib and mascot.

### Run one

To explore all functions before adapting a single scenario, open the bundled
app that shows every function, from an interactive R console:

```r
mascot::mascot_example("studio")
```

Or run a copied example's directory with `shiny::runApp()`. The call waits until
the app closes; locating the file with `run = FALSE` does not launch it.

```{r mascot_example-host-mode, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
if (in_studio()) cat("In the studio, selecting this function opens the Examples host mode. Run the launch call you copy there in your R console; the host does not start another app.\n")
```

```{r mascot_example-mistakes, echo = FALSE}
if (!in_studio()) guide_mistakes_html("mascot_example", studio_character)
```
